review_notes: I read the whole file's structure and checked the large near-duplicate pairs. I compared T1F3_finBound with T1F3_finBound_set, T1J_bound with T1J_bound_unif, and the T1F5_* lemmas with the WhitEntire.* lemmas. I did not compile anything. In finding 1, the replacement proof sketch assumes the set-membership hypotheses unify by `Set.mem_setOf_eq`. T1F3_finBound_set would also have to move before T1F3_finBound and take F explicitly, because it currently sits in T1Main under `variable (F)`. Only the two lemma statements in finding 2 were checked by hand, so their typing is unconfirmed. Other parallel pairs, such as the real and complex variants and the `_unif` versions of T1AR/T1AC, were left out because their differing types would make a shared lemma awkward.

findings.problem: T1F3_finBound (about 170 lines) and T1F3_finBound_set (lines 2526–2697) have essentially the same proof. Both build Nf and hNfin and pick the ideal I and the constants c₀ and CL. Both define x, eξ, eu and hvalx, and both prove hsupp, hprod, hvan, hplace, hMprod, hfin1, hfin2 and the final calc. The only difference is that T1F3_finBound fixes the bound ‖s‖ ≤ R and extracts (M, κ) from hΦb R, while T1F3_finBound_set takes M, κ and an arbitrary set T of parameters up front. The set version is strictly more general, so any change to the shared argument must be made twice.
findings.proposed_change: Keep only the general lemma T1F3_finBound_set. It must be moved before T1F3_finBound, into the FinBound section with an explicit F. Then prove T1F3_finBound as a short corollary: `obtain ⟨M, κ, hM, hb⟩ := hΦb R; obtain ⟨I, c, hc0, h⟩ := T1F3_finBound_set F S thr hthr L hLfin hL0 M κ hM; exact ⟨κ, I, c, hc0, fun j s hs uf huf ξ => h n Φ {s' | ‖s'‖ ≤ R} hΦ1 hΦ0 (fun j v w e s' hs' hw => hb j v w e s' hs' hw) j s hs uf huf ξ⟩`. The caller at line 2355 stays unchanged. T1F3_finBound's statement already bundles n, Φ and the hypotheses as arguments, so the corollary fits its signature.
findings.benefit: This removes about 170 lines of duplicated valuation, finprod and norm-bound reasoning, and leaves a single place to maintain the Euler-factor local bound. A reader sees that the R-version is the T = ball case of the set version.

findings.problem: T1J_bound (2309–2495) and T1J_bound_unif (2923 to the end) repeat the same assembly step. Both set up PR, PC, MX, MR, MC and the nonnegativity facts hPR0, hPC0, hMX0, hMR0 and hMC0. Both apply WE_absorb, then run the `hterm` chain h1..h4: `mul_le_mul (hCb j) hKcb …`, then `mul_le_mul h1 (hARb j) …`, and so on, with the n1..n4 nonnegativity side goals. Both finish with the same `hJ … := rfl`, `norm_mul`, `hν`, `hcpb`, `norm_sum_le` and `ring` steps. The only difference is that D·Tm^B replaces |BC j| in the unif version, so the constants differ. About 100 lines of nontrivial inequality bookkeeping are therefore maintained twice.
findings.proposed_change: Extract a purely real/complex lemma for the five-factor product bound, stated roughly as: `lemma norm_mul₅_le {z₁ z₂ z₃ z₄ z₅ : ℂ} {b₁ b₂ b₃ b₄ b₅ : ℝ} (h₁ : ‖z₁‖ ≤ b₁) … (h₅ : ‖z₅‖ ≤ b₅) (n₁ : 0 ≤ b₁) (n₂ : 0 ≤ b₂) (n₃ : 0 ≤ b₃) (n₄ : 0 ≤ b₄) : ‖z₁*z₂*z₃*z₄*z₅‖ ≤ b₁*b₂*b₃*b₄*b₅`. The proof is `norm_mul` four times plus `mul_le_mul` chained. Then add a second lemma that combines it with habsorb: if `MR*MC ≤ cabs*PR*PC` and the constants are nonnegative, then `b₁*(bR*MR)*(bC*MC)*(cF*MX) ≤ (b₁*bR*bC*cF*cabs)*(PR*PC*MX)`. Both `hterm` blocks then become one `have := norm_mul₅_le …; exact this.trans (by … )` call, with only the constants (|BC j| versus C0, and DR·Tm^… versus plain DR) supplied separately.
findings.benefit: The shared inequality chain would be proved once, so the fragile nonnegativity side goals sit in one place. Each main bound theorem would show only how its own constants (|BC j| versus C0, DR versus DR^rR·Tm^…) are chosen. That would shorten both T1J_bound proofs considerably.

findings.problem: T1F5_one_add_mul_rpow_neg_le has the same statement and proof as WhitEntire.one_add_mul_rpow_neg_le. T1F5_dilation_bound_of_polyDecay and its complex variant (lines 1237–1285) repeat the argument of WhitEntire.dilation_bound_real and dilation_bound_complex, which is the `ht₀`/`hζ₀`, `hge`, `h1`, `h2` and final `calc` pattern with A = 0. A search found no uses of the two dilation lemmas apart from the T1F5 one_add lemma inside them. They are dead copies of the WhitEntire versions, and the three-line `hge`/`h1`/`h2` core is also repeated inside the real and complex WhitEntire lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Delete lines 1226–1285 (the T1F5 `one_add_mul_rpow_neg_le` and the two unused T1F5 dilation lemmas) and keep only WhitEntire.one_add_mul_rpow_neg_le and WhitEntire.dilation_bound_real/complex. If an A = 0 form is ever needed, derive it from `WhitEntire.dilation_bound_real` by applying it with A = 0 and `pow_zero`. In the WhitEntire lemmas, optionally factor out the shared step `1 + ‖t‖ ≥ 1 + κ·(r‖x‖)` followed by `one_add_mul_rpow_neg_le` into one lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes about 60 lines of dead, duplicated analytic reasoning, so there is one authoritative copy of the polynomial-decay-under-dilation estimate.
